question: Which drug is the definitive treatment for malignant hyperthermia (MH) triggered by volatile anaesthetic agents?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Neostigmine reverses non-depolarising neuromuscular blockade; it has no role in treating MH.

Correct. Dantrolene sodium (2.5 mg/kg IV, repeated as needed) is the only specific pharmacological treatment for MH; it blocks ryanodine receptor-mediated calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Haloperidol is an antipsychotic with no role in MH management.
Propranolol may be used for associated arrhythmias but is not the definitive treatment; it does not address the underlying calcium dysregulation.

overallFeedback.feedback: The definitive treatment for malignant hyperthermia is dantrolene sodium 2.5 mg/kg IV. Immediately stop all triggering agents and call for help.
Excellent. Dantrolene is the only drug that directly counters MH by blocking pathological calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
